name: Chouara Tannery
hero_subtitle: Stone vats of dye and leather drying on the rooftops, much as it has for centuries.

overview.title: A Medieval Workshop Still at Work
overview.p1: Chouara is the largest and most famous tannery in Fes, and its way of working has changed very little since the Middle Ages. Hides are soaked, scraped and dyed by hand in a honeycomb of round stone vats, then laid out on the rooftops to dry in the sun.
overview.p2: You watch from the terraces of the surrounding leather shops, reached through narrow lanes. Staff will often hand you a sprig of mint to hold to your nose, because the smell is strong. There's no fee for the view, but the shops hope you'll browse, so decide beforehand what you're comfortable with and keep it friendly. Mornings show the vats at their busiest.

moods.title: What to See at the Chouara Tannery
moods.subtitle: A short visit with a strong impression.

1.title: The Dye Pits
1.desc: Rows of round stone vats in earthy reds, yellows and blues, worked by men standing waist-deep.

2.title: Leather Shop Terraces
2.desc: Choose a terrace with a clear view, take your mint, and feel free to say no thanks afterwards.

3.title: Bags, Jackets & Slippers
3.desc: If you want leather goods, compare a few shops and bargain politely. Quality varies.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Chouara Tannery

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: It is in the northeast of the medina. Follow signs to Chouara or go with a guide, since the lanes are confusing.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Go in the morning, when the vats are busiest and the light is best. Midday sun can make the smell stronger.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: Hold the mint to your nose if the smell bothers you. Shops expect you to look, not buy. Be polite, agree on prices before accepting help and ask before photographing workers.

q1.question: Is the Chouara Tannery free to visit?
q1.answer: The view is free, but the leather shops with terraces hope you'll browse. A small tip is common.

q2.question: What is the best time to see the tannery?
q2.answer: Morning, when work is at its busiest and the light is best.

q3.question: Does the tannery smell bad?
q3.answer: The smell is strong. You'll usually be offered mint leaves to hold to your nose, which helps.

q4.question: Can I take photos?
q4.answer: Yes, from the terraces. Ask before photographing workers up close.
